First diff cmd/cmd.go: PullHandler bar creation: previously bar = progress.NewBar(fmt.Sprintf("pulling %s...", resp.Digest[7:19]), resp.Total, resp.Completed). Now 0. Might be bug? Also they changed digest display to full digest? Previously 7:19 = 12 chars. Now full digest? Trim prefix gives full hex. Might be okay but progress bar start at 0 not completed? Could be intentional to reset? Hmm.

Also progress bar creation uses resp.Total, resp.Completed previously. Now 0. Might be bug: should start at resp.Completed? Might be okay if bar is created first time, completed should be 0. But resp.Completed may be >0? Hmm.

Second cache/blob/cache.go: comment change. Resolve comment changed. Removed TODO. Link comment removed TODO. Links comment changed. checkWriter struct fields reordered, added w io.Writer. Write method now checks err early, writes to w instead of f. Previously wrote to f. Now w is set by creator. In copyNamedFile, they set w: f. So okay.

But checkWriter has fields d, size, f, h, w, n, err. Previously d, size, n, h, f, err. Now n after w. Write uses w.Write. Good.

Potential bug: checkWriter.Write now does not update n? It does w.n += int64(n). Good.

But checkWriter.Write previously wrote to h then f. Now writes to h then w. Good.

Potential issue: checkWriter has f *os.File // nil means pre-validated in Chunker. In Chunker.Put, they create checkWriter with f: c.f, w: io.NewOffsetWriter(c.f, chunk.Start). So f is set but w is offset writer. Write will hash and write to offset writer. Good.

But checkWriter also has field f unused? Might be leftover.

Also nameToPath removed check for "@". Previously returned errInvalidName if contains "@". Now removed. Might be intentional? The comment about Resolve says forms: @<digest>, <name>@<digest>, <name>. So name may contain @? Hmm.

splitNameDigest presumably splits at @? Let's see not shown. Might be okay.

absJoin panic message changed.

chunked.go new file. Chunker struct has digest, size, f. Chunked returns &Chunker{} if file exists and size matches. That's pre-validated. Put returns nil if c.f == nil. Good.

Potential bug: Chunked returns &Chunker{} with zero values, but digest and size not set. Put checks c.f == nil, returns nil. That's fine.

But Close() returns c.f.Close() which will panic if f nil. Should check nil. Might be bug.

Also Chunked returns error if os.OpenFile fails. Good.

In registry.go: DefaultChunkingThreshold changed from 128<<20 to 64<<20. MaxChunkSize removed. MaxStreams negative means no limit? Previously maxStreams returned max(n,2). Now just cmp.Or. Could cause deadlock? Might be intentional.

Pull method changed significantly. Previously parsed name extended, then resolve, then for each layer, if exists skip, else create request, etc. Now they resolve first, then for each layer they check exists, then create chunker, then iterate chunksums. They removed scheme parsing before resolve? They parse inside chunksums.

Potential bug: they removed scheme, n parsing before resolve, but resolve uses name. Okay.

They changed progress tracking: they send initial trace events with 0. Then skip if exists. Then for each layer they create chunker, defer chunked.Close(). Defer inside loop? That's problematic: defer will run at function exit, not per iteration. If many layers, many defers accumulate. Might be okay but could hold files open. Better to close immediately. Also defer inside loop with errgroup may cause many open files.

Also they set skip[i] = true if exists, then t.update(l, l.Size, ErrCached). Then later they skip iteration. Good.

But they also call t.update(l,0,nil) for all layers before checking exists. Might be okay.

Potential bug: progress tracking uses atomic.Int64 per layer? They have var progress atomic.Int64 per layer iteration, but they reuse same variable? It's defined inside for loop per layer, so each layer gets its own. Good.

But trackingReader uses n *atomic.Int64. They create body := &trackingReader{r: res.Body, n: &progress}. Then chunked.Put(cs.Chunk, cs.Digest, body). Put will copy N bytes via io.CopyN. trackingReader.Read will add bytes read to progress. Good.

But they also update trace via t.update(l, progress.Load(), err) in defer. Might be okay.

Potential bug: they never check if layer size is zero? Not.

Chunksums function: returns iter.Seq2. For small layers (< threshold), they yield one chunksum with URL built from scheme, n.Host etc. Chunk start 0 end l.Size-1. Digest = l.Digest. Good.

For large layers, they fetch chunksums endpoint. They parse response with bufio.Scanner ScanWords. They expect digest then chunk range. They parse digest via blob.ParseDigest(s.Bytes()). Then parse chunk via chunks.Parse(s.Bytes()). Good.
